title: Onboard assay: implementation notes for model eval scripts and CI
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a practical, implementation-first companion for onboarding new models into the evals/assay pipeline. Focus: small runnable scripts, dataset loader patterns, scoring function recipes, and pragmatic CI wiring for regression detection. Not a design doc — this is the playbook engineers will copy/paste from during model onboarding.

Quick start (minimal):
- clone evals-harness repo, create feature branch: git checkout -b onboard/<model>-assay
- add assay under assays/<model>/<assay_name>/ (see layout below)
- run: python -m assays.<model>.<assay_name>.run --local --seed 42 --sample 100
- push branch and open PR with artifacts (metrics CSV, example failures)

Repo/layout recommendation (concrete):
- assays/<model-name>/<assay-slug>/
  - data/ (original dataset + small fixtures used in unit tests)
  - loaders.py (dataset loader + streaming iterator)
  - scoring.py (per-example scoring + aggregator)
  - run.py (CLI wrapper to run end-to-end)
  - smoke_inputs.json (5–10 hand-picked cases)
  - README.md (short: what question this assay answers + expected pass metric)

Dataset loader patterns: practical tips
- single responsibility: loader returns a generator of normalized examples (dicts with keys question, context, expected, metadata)
- deterministic shuffling: expose seed param and use numpy.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle on index array not on list in-place if parallel workers will read offsets
- streaming vs in-memory: for large corpora, implement a streaming parser with checkpointable offsets (line+byte offset or record index) so CI can sample smaller slices quickly
- canonical schema mapping: have a small mapping table at top of loader for field aliases (e.g., {"prompt": "question", "input": "context"}) to handle variant datasets without changing scoring code
- fast dev mode: provide loader(sample=10) to return a tiny deterministic subset using fixed seed (used by pre-submit tests)
- fixture generation helper: scripts/generate_fixtures.py to create smoke_inputs.json and a failing_case_examples.json for manual triage

Example loader sketch (plaintext):
# loaders.py
def load_examples(path, sample=None, seed=42):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    with open(path) as f:
        for i, line in enumerate(f):
            # parse jsonl or csv row -> normalize dict
            yield normalized_example

Scoring functions: recipes and pitfalls
- Two layers: per-example scorer -> aggregator. Always return both raw score(s) and a status label (pass|fail|warn).
- Deterministic tasks: use exact-match or normalized exact-match (strip punctuation, lowercase, normalize whitespace). Provide fuzzy-match threshold when answers can be multi-token.
- Generation tasks: prefer log-prob based scoring for calibration checks; use n-gram and token-level metrics when quality requires it (ROUGE-L for long answers, token-F1 for extraction).
- Probabilistic outputs: expose top-k logprobs and normalized probabilities. Compute expected calibration error (ECE) buckets for confidence checks.
- Regression sensitivity: define delta thresholds (absolute + relative). Example: accept up to 1.5% drop in EM but require manual review if >1.5% and <3%.
- Avoid brittle heuristics: don’t rely on string equality for date/time answers — instead parse canonical forms (ISO) before compare.

Scoring snippet (plaintext):
# scoring.py
def exact_match(pred, gold):
    p = normalize(pred)
    g = normalize(gold)
    return 1.0 if p == g else 0.0

def token_f1(pred, gold):
    p_tokens = tokenize(pred)
    g_tokens = tokenize(gold)
    prec = intersection(p_tokens,g_tokens)/len(p_tokens) if p_tokens else 0
    rec = intersection(p_tokens,g_tokens)/len(g_tokens) if g_tokens else 0
    if prec+rec==0: return 0.0
    return 2*prec*rec/(prec+rec)

CI wiring (practical, incremental):
- Principle: fast, cheap gate + nightly heavy runs + full regression alerts to owners.
- Pre-submit (fast): run unit tests for loaders + smoke run with sample=10 and the model stub (mock logits) to ensure code paths exercise scoring. Time budget: <60s.
- Merge gate (medium): run assay end-to-end on small shard (100 examples) against a stable baseline model (pinned model version in workflow) and compute core metrics. Fail CI if metric crosses hard threshold (configurable per assay). Time budget: ~5–10 min.
- Nightly/regression (heavy): full dataset + multiple seeds + multiple temperature settings, store metrics CSV in artifacts bucket and compare against previous baseline. If drift detected beyond threshold, create JIRA regression issue with attached failure examples.

Suggested GitHub Actions matrix (text):
- job: assay-test
  strategy:
    matrix:
      mode: [smoke, shard]
      python: [3.10]
  steps: checkout, setup, run smoke runner (python run.py --mode ${{matrix.mode}})

Artifact policy and artifacts to store:
- always upload: metrics.csv, failures_sample.jsonl (N=50), example_responses.zip (N=20)
- for nightly: full_metrics.parquet, per-seed breakdown, profiling trace (cpu/gpu)
- retention policy: 30 days for merge-run artifacts, 90 days for nightly baselines

Testing checklist (copy into PR template):
- [ ] loader unit tests (schema mapping, sample param, streaming behavior)
- [ ] scoring unit tests (edge cases: empty output, extra punctuation, numeric formats)
- [ ] smoke_inputs.csv included and referenced in README
- [ ] local run completes with sample=10 under 30s
- [ ] baseline metrics attached to PR if this is a new assay

Performance & cost notes:
- quantify token budget: sample=100 end-to-end cost estimate = prompt_tokens * model_cost + output_tokens * model_cost (put rough numbers in README)
- use caching for repeated model calls in unit tests: a small in-repo cache layer that returns stored outputs to avoid repeated costs during CI
- KV-cache fixtures: for decoder-only models, include cached KV states when we need to simulate long-context behavior without re-generating prefixes

Debugging and triage tips:
- failures_sample.jsonl should include: input, expected, predicted, logits/topk, score breakdown, seed, model_version
- create minimal reproducer scripts: reproduce_failure.py --case-id <id> --model <version> --seed 123
- when comparing across model variants, canonicalize tokenization differences by mapping canonical_ids when possible

Operational escalation and owners:
- each assay must list an owner in README (person or team). Default owner: eng-applied-ml
- on regression alert: auto-create JIRA with label assay-regression and tag owner. Attach: metrics diff, top 10 failures, profiling trace.

Open questions / TODOs (for triage during onboarding):
- Decide canonical thresholding rules per task family (classification, extraction, generation) — draft proposal needed (JIRA-ML-789).
- Consolidate lightweight model stubs we use in pre-submit (GPU-free) — PR to create stub image.
- Improve synthetic fixture generator to produce adversarial negatives for extraction tasks.

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc emphasizes pragmatic, copy-paste friendly patterns rather than architecture theory. If you have an existing assay template we should adopt, link it here and I will rework to match.
- If you add a new scoring metric, please include a short justification and a small unit test that shows a pathological example it catches.

References and real links (examples to copy):
- github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-harness (main repo)
- ex. PR for smoke-run workflow: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-harness/pull/482

Quick TODO for this doc:
- [ ] attach example run artifacts (metrics CSV + failure examples)
- [ ] add concrete GitHub Actions YAML and runner image reference
- [ ] standardize metric names used across assays (EM, F1, ROUGE-L, ECE)

End.
